subject: POC onramp: commissioning cadence, keys, IP allowlist & peering
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@cardiovera.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 02 Apr 2029 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: POC onramp: commissioning cadence, keys, IP allowlist & peering

Hi Liam —

Great to have CardioVera in an evaluation with Redwood. Attached is a concise Mutual Action Plan (MAP) that lays out the commissioning cadence we typically follow for a 4-week POC. The MAP focuses on the items you flagged: org setup, API keys, IP allowlist, and optional VPC peering.

High level proposed cadence (week-by-week):
- Week 0 (today–end of week): Org & SSO setup, billing contact, basic onboarding call
- Week 1: API key issuance, initial test ingest, baseline latency/cost trace
- Week 2: IP allowlist + ephemeral key rotation for staging; sample inference traffic
- Week 3: Optional VPC peering (if you want private networking), performance run, simple integration test
- Week 4: Acceptance checklist, handover notes, and next steps for Dedicated or Private if you choose to continue

Ask for you: please confirm whether Procurement needs a separate PO window and if networking will require peering (we can keep it optional to accelerate launch). I copied Neha for security/compliance and Jonas for network details — they’ll own the technical artifacts.

Attachments: MAP-CardioVera-v1.0.pdf (mutual action plan), vpc-peering-diagram.png (optional topology), api-key-sample.txt (example key naming convention).

Proposed quick next step: 30-minute kickoff tomorrow 10:00–10:30am PT to confirm owners and sign the MAP. If that works I’ll share a calendar invite.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
Redwood Inference

From: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@cardiovera.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 02 Apr 2029 12:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: POC onramp: commissioning cadence, keys, IP allowlist & peering

Hi Marissa —

Thanks — the MAP looks sensible and the timeline is aggressive but doable. A couple quick clarifications from our side before we lock kickoff:
1) Procurement: we can sign a short MSA addendum and a one-month trial PO; procurement wants final pricing and a point of contact for invoicing (I’ll loop them separately).
2) IP allowlist: we’ll start with allowlist-only for staging. Peering is a hard requirement only if we see a latency/security gap during week 2/3.
3) Org setup: we use Okta; do you support SCIM for user provisioning or will we rely on manual invites?

Can do tomorrow 10:00am PT for the kickoff. I’ll include our platform lead in the calendar.

Cheers,
Liam O'Connor
Head of Cloud Ops, CardioVera
liam.oconnor@cardiovera.com

Subject: Re: POC onramp: commissioning cadence, keys, IP allowlist & peering

Thanks Liam — great. Quick answers:
- Pricing/invoicing: I’ll send a short cost summary to Procurement after the kickoff and include our billing contact.
- SCIM / Okta: Redwood supports SAML and SCIM for org provisioning on Private/Dedicated. For hosted POC we can enable SCIM provisioning if you want a quick user sync; otherwise manual invites work. Jonas — can you note the SCIM play?
- IP allowlist workflow: we’ll provide a CIDR list (e.g., 34.120.0.0/20) and a short runbook to add to your firewall. Neha will validate the retention/audit wording in the MAP.

I’ll send the invite for 10:00am PT and prepare a short kickoff agenda (20m technical, 10m commercial).

Marissa

Hi all —

Quick security notes ahead of kickoff:
- For the POC we recommend: short-lived API keys (30d), enforced TLS, and IP allowlist for staging.
- Retention: we will not persist customer input beyond the POC snapshot unless you opt in; logs retained per MAP for 30 days by default.
- Evidence: I attached the one-page security checklist and SOC2 summary to speed Procurement/SecOps review.

Jonas — if CardioVera wants VPC peering, I can coordinate the shared bucket test and get the peering CIDR approval checklist ready.

See attachments: security-checklist.pdf, SOC2-summary.pdf.

Neha Kapoor
Security Lead, Redwood Inference

Kickoff was helpful. Procurement confirms they can issue a one-month trial PO; I’ve asked them to send terms to Marissa. We’ll start with allowlist-only for staging; if network tests show issues we’ll greenlight VPC peering in week 2. SCIM would be ideal for us — please include SCIM enablement in week 0 tasks.

Action items we own: add the staging firewall entries (tomorrow), share Okta admin for SCIM integration, and confirm billing contact.
Action items for Redwood: send final MAP v1.1 with Neha’s retention language included, provide API key when work account is provisioned, and the peering checklist if we decide to proceed.

Thanks — looking forward to this moving fast.
